comment: Building elevations with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimensions are not provided. Plan view only shows OHE line locations without vertical clearance data needed to verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductors to building faces.
applicableAreas: buildings near overhead electric lines on southern and eastern boundaries

comment: The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies to all customer facilities. No profile, section, or elevation views are provided showing radial clearance measurements from outside conductors to building footprints, parking areas, or other site features in three dimensions.
applicableAreas: customer facilities near overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors on southern and eastern boundaries

comment: No building elevation sheets are provided showing building projections relative to overhead conductors. Without elevation views detailing overhang, awning, balcony, or roof projections and their clearances from overhead lines, compliance with both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies) near overhead electric facilities

comment: Overhead electric facilities exist in the ROW adjacent to the site (along Valley View Road, western boundary). Buildings are proposed on site, but surveyed clearance dimensions from buildings to these facilities are not provided on elevation or section views to demonstrate permanent clearance requirements are met.
applicableAreas: buildings near electric facilities in right-of-way adjacent to site

comment: No building elevation sheets are included in the 39-sheet site plan set. Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimensioned clearances are required to demonstrate compliance with clearance requirements when buildings are within potential clearance distance of overhead facilities.
applicableAreas: all buildings and elevated structures near overhead facilities

comment: No section or profile views are provided showing dimensions from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of buildings and building projections. Site plan shows buildings near overhead lines but lacks dimensioned clearance verification exhibits required by code.
applicableAreas: all buildings and building projections within potential clearance distance of overhead facilities

comment: Retaining walls are proposed on the site (up to 14 feet height per Sheet 38). Walls are shown on the site plan near the southern and eastern property boundaries where overhead lines exist. However, no section views showing vertical clearance dimensions from the outer electric line conductor to the wall faces are provided to verify the 7.5-foot clearance requirement.
applicableAreas: retaining walls on southern and eastern boundaries near overhead lines

comment: Retaining walls are proposed near overhead electric lines on the southern and eastern boundaries. Section exhibits showing dimensions from outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of wall faces for clearance verification are not provided. Wall sections show structural details but lack clearance dimension callouts referencing conductor locations.
applicableAreas: retaining walls on southern and eastern boundaries within clearance distance of overhead lines

comment: Driveways and parking areas are proposed throughout the site. Grading plan shows finished floor elevations for buildings and finished grade in parking areas. However, no surveyed mid-span clearance measurements are provided showing the lowest point of overhead lines (including any attached equipment) relative to driveway and parking surface elevations. Determination of whether truck traffic will use driveways to establish 16-foot vs. 18-foot requirement is not explicitly documented.
applicableAreas: driveways and parking areas throughout site

comment: Site plan shows internal driveways and parking layout. Overhead utility poles (part of OHE line configuration) exist on the site. The plan does not explicitly show pole relocation or notes indicating whether poles within 30 feet of driveway edges have been relocated. Without surveyed pole locations and driveway alignment dimensions, conflict determination cannot be definitively made.
applicableAreas: driveways near electric poles

comment: No clearance dimensions are provided on any site plan sheets showing measurements from the outside conductor (outermost electric line) to buildings, structures, walls, or other site features. Where clearance dimensions should be shown (such as on building elevation sheets or section views), none are present. The measurement standard (from outside conductor, not from pole centerline) cannot be verified because no dimensions are shown.
applicableAreas: all clearance dimensions on site plan

comment: Electric easements (5-foot electric easements and 7.5-foot PUE per plat dedication) are shown on site plan. Overhead distribution facilities exist within and adjacent to these easement areas. Site features (buildings, walls, parking) are shown in proximity to these easements, but clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to items within the easement are not provided. The absolute prohibition against facilities under or over distribution lines, as distinct from the 7.5-foot clearance requirement, cannot be verified without elevation data showing vertical spatial relationships.
applicableAreas: all buildings and site features within electric easements on southern and eastern boundaries

comment: Driveway and parking area elevations are shown on the grading plan. Overhead electric facilities exist on the site. No registered surveyor mid-span clearance data is provided showing the vertical distance from the lowest point of overhead conductors (including any attached equipment like transformers) to proposed driveway and parking surface elevations. When vertical clearance appears marginal based on available data, surveyor-certified field measurements of mid-span clearances are required.
applicableAreas: driveways and parking areas throughout site

comment: Landscape plan shows 3 mitigation trees (marked 'M') positioned within 10 lateral feet of the overhead electric line (-OHE-) on the southern property boundary. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees within 50 lateral feet of transmission lines (or 10 lateral feet of distribution lines) to be from the Utility Compatible Shade Trees list (ECM Appendix F, species marked UC with mature height generally ≤20 feet). The plant list (Sheet 35) identifies proposed shade trees as Live Oak and Cedar Elm, and ornamental trees as Texas Mountain Laurel and Mexican Redbud, but does not explicitly verify that any of these species are marked utility-compatible or that the specific 3 mitigation trees near the overhead line are one of these approved species. No species identification is provided for the 3 mitigation trees shown on the landscape plan near the overhead lines.
applicableAreas: 3 mitigation trees on southern property boundary within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors

comment: Down guy wires from distribution poles may exist on the site but are not clearly depicted on the survey or site plan. The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) includes a legend item for 'guy wires' but the plan view does not explicitly show down guy wire locations or their relationship to proposed accessible paths and driveways. Without explicit down guy location mapping, potential conflicts cannot be definitively identified or resolved. Electric utility infrastructure, including guy wire systems, is frequently omitted from site plans per the grouping's common violation patterns.
applicableAreas: pedestrian pathways and driveways throughout site

comment: Down guy anchor locations (if they exist) are not explicitly mapped on the site plan or easement exhibits. The survey legend includes guy wire symbols but these are not clearly identified on the survey drawing. Without explicit down guy anchor point locations with associated 10-foot-wide and 5-foot-extension easement boundaries shown on an easement exhibit, compliance with this documentation requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: if down guy anchors from distribution poles exist on site

comment: Transformers (pole-mounted or pad-mounted) are shown on the electrical design plan (Sheet 21). Overhead lines exist on the site. However, no vertical clearance dimensions are provided showing the distance from overhead line conductors to the top of transformer equipment. Without elevation views and clearance dimension callouts, the 7.5-foot vertical sky-to-ground clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: transformers shown on electrical plan

comment: No construction logistics plan, site logistics plan, or construction phasing plan is included in the submitted site plan set that maps construction staging areas, equipment laydown zones, crane swing radius, or work platforms. Without these plans showing staging area boundaries with 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines maintained during construction, the working clearance requirement (OSHA 1910.333, UCM § 1.10.2) cannot be verified to be satisfied.
applicableAreas: construction staging areas, equipment laydown, crane operations

comment: The required note stating 'Owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines' per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 is not included on the cover sheet or general notes sheets. This notification requirement is mandatory when overhead electric lines exist on or adjacent to a site with construction activities. The absence of this critical safety note from the plan set is non-compliant.
applicableAreas: entire site, all construction activities

comment: Mitigation trees proposed near the overhead electric distribution line are not identified by species on the landscape plan. Species identification is required to verify utility compatibility per ECM Appendix F. Identify tree species for all trees within 25 feet of the overhead distribution conductor and cross-reference to ECM Appendix F to verify utility-compatible designation.
applicableAreas: southern property boundary near overhead electric line (OHE)

comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated from smaller trees on the landscape plan. The plan cannot be used to verify that large trees are maintained beyond the 25-foot clearance zone from the distribution conductor. Identify mature height classifications for all proposed trees and show clearance dimensions to confirm compliance.
applicableAreas: southern property boundary near overhead electric line

comment: Utility pole locations are not identified on the landscape plan. Without specific pole locations plotted, the distance from proposed trees to poles cannot be verified. Show utility pole locations and add dimension lines demonstrating minimum 10-foot lateral clearance from tree trunk center to pole.
applicableAreas: southern property boundary along OHE

comment: Pad-mounted transformer and electrical equipment locations are not shown on the landscape plan. Without equipment locations visible for comparison with tree locations, clearance distances cannot be verified. Overlay electrical equipment locations on the landscape plan and dimension the clearance from tree trunk center to equipment access door (minimum 10 feet).
applicableAreas: pad-mounted transformer locations

comment: Underground electrical equipment locations are not shown on the landscape plan. Show underground utility locations (pull boxes, vaults, equipment) and dimension minimum 5-foot lateral clearance from tree trunk center.
applicableAreas: underground electrical infrastructure areas

comment: Root barrier requirements for trees within 20 feet of underground equipment cannot be verified without equipment locations shown on the landscape plan. Identify underground equipment, mark 20-foot clearance radius, and show root barrier specifications (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) for affected trees.
applicableAreas: underground electrical equipment areas within 20-foot tree planting radius

comment: The landscape plan legend identifies trees only by functional category (SY, PL, P, M), not by species. Species names must be added to the landscape plan legend or directly adjacent to tree symbols to allow reviewers to verify utility compatibility per ECM Appendix F. Update landscape plan to show species names for all trees, particularly those proposed within 25 feet of overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: landscape plan, all tree locations, particularly trees near overhead electric facilities

comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) are not differentiated on the landscape plan, making it impossible to verify clearance compliance. Add notation on the landscape plan indicating mature height category for trees near overhead electric facilities (e.g., 'L' for large trees 40+ feet, 'S' for small trees <40 feet), or add mature height specification directly on the plan adjacent to each tree symbol.
applicableAreas: landscape plan, all tree locations

comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan. Add dimension lines from the outer conductor position (not pole centerline) to tree trunk center, clearly identifying the measurement reference point and demonstrating compliance with minimum lateral distances.
applicableAreas: near overhead electric line

comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan. Add dimension lines from the outer conductor position to tree trunk center (not projected canopy edge), clearly terminating at the planting location symbol to demonstrate compliance.
applicableAreas: near overhead electric line

comment: Cannot verify whether proposed trees are within prohibited clearance zones due to lack of species identification and distance measurements. If trees proposed within restricted zones (per species/height/distance analysis) are approved, provide documented written approval from Austin Energy authorizing the exception.
applicableAreas: mitigation trees near overhead electric line

comment: Transformer Pads 2 and 3 are located immediately adjacent to building walls with visual clearance estimated at only 2-5 feet, falling significantly short of the required 5-foot minimum clearance from brick/masonry buildings per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4. No dimensions are marked on the electrical plan to verify clearance compliance.
applicableAreas: Pad 2 (west of Building 2, Unit 201)
Pad 3 (west of Building 8, Unit 801)

comment: Retaining walls are shown on the grading plan (Sheet 11) around the site perimeter and pond, but their relationship to transformer pad locations cannot be determined from the plans because (1) transformer pads are not shown on the grading plan, and (2) no clearance dimensions are marked. Applicability depends on whether any pad is located within 5 feet of a retaining wall.
applicableAreas: Not determinable from current plan set

comment: No fences or gates are shown on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) adjacent to transformer pads. The site plan (Sheet 9) does not show fences at transformer pad locations. Without fences shown on the plans, this requirement is not applicable. However, if fences are proposed in the landscape or site plan, the clearance requirements (5 feet for sides with operators/controls, 3 feet for sides without) must be verified.
applicableAreas: Not determinable from current plan set

comment: The electrical plan shows Pads 2 and 3 with approximately 2-5 feet clearance to buildings, which would trigger the reduced clearance exception if the applicant intends to claim it. However, there is no documentation of (1) Austin Energy Design written approval, (2) verification that location is not in confined space, (3) adequate clearance to windows/doors/ducts (10 ft+ requirement), (4) adequate vertical clearance to windows/doors (15 ft+ requirement), or (5) 3-hour fire rating for the clearance area. Without architectural specifications showing fire ratings or AE Design approval letter, compliance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Pad 2 and Pad 3 (if reduced clearances are proposed)

comment: No balconies or building overhangs are visible on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) or site plan (Sheet 9) located directly above or immediately adjacent to any of the five transformer pads. The requirement applies only 'when balconies or overhangs are present above or adjacent to transformer.' Building elevations would be needed to confirm whether overhangs extend over pad locations. This cannot be verified from the current plan set.
applicableAreas: Not determinable from current plan set

comment: The electrical plan does not identify whether transformer equipment is oil-filled or dry-type, which triggers different clearance requirements. Building elevations showing window/door locations and their heights are not provided in the plan set. Without (1) equipment type specification, (2) building elevation drawings, and (3) measured distances from pads to windows/doors, the 12-foot clearance requirement for oil-filled equipment cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: The site plan (Sheet 9) shows concrete sidewalks as part of the site infrastructure, but no sidewalks are explicitly shown on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) positioned adjacent to transformer pads. The location of site sidewalks relative to each transformer pad cannot be clearly determined from the available plans. Dimensions from pads to nearby sidewalk back-of-curb lines are not marked.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: No stairwells serving as fire exits are shown on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) adjacent to transformer pad locations. Building floor plans are not provided in the plan set. The requirement applies only 'when stairwells are present adjacent to transformer.' Without building floor plans showing stair locations, this cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Not determinable from current plan set

comment: The electrical plan does not specify whether transformer equipment is oil-filled or dry-type, and no fire escape locations are identified on the plans. The site plan (Sheet 9) does not show fire escapes or stairs serving as fire escapes. Building elevations are not provided. Without equipment type specification and without identification of fire escape locations, the 20-foot horizontal/radial clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if oil-filled)

comment: The electrical plan does not mark or specify access door orientation for any of the five transformer pads, making it impossible to verify that hot-stick use areas have minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent buildings. This is a required documentation element—transformer pad symbols must indicate which side is the access door, and clearance zones must be dimensioned or clearly marked.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pads

comment: The electrical plan does not provide cross-sections or detail drawings showing whether any transformer pad is located in a niche, vault, or enclosed area on three or more sides (confined space configuration). Without cross-section drawings demonstrating either 35-foot vertical clearance (if niche) or confirmation that the location is not confined space, the 15-foot versus 10-foot clearance requirement cannot be determined.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if in confined space)

comment: The fire protection plan (Sheet 10) shows fire hydrant locations on the site, and the electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations, but the two plans do not cross-reference transformer pad positions relative to fire hydrants. No dimensions are marked from any pad to the nearest hydrant. Without explicit distance callouts, compliance with the 5-foot minimum clearance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if fire hydrants adjacent)

comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not label or identify transformer pad locations, making it impossible to assess whether trees within 10 lateral feet of any pad or trees within 15 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors are present. The landscape plan provides a tree/plant legend but does not cross-reference tree species to transformer locations. Without this cross-reference and without the landscape plan showing transformer pads, the utility-compatibility requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: The landscape plan does not depict transformer pad locations, making it impossible to verify the spacing of shrubs or low-lying vegetation relative to transformer access door sides (10 ft minimum) versus other sides (5 ft minimum). Without transformer pads shown on the landscape plan and without dimension callouts from plantings to pad locations, this requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not show transformer pad locations, and no root barrier details are visible or cross-referenced with transformer locations. Without transformer pads identified on the landscape plan, it is impossible to verify whether trees within 20 lateral feet of any pad have root barriers specified (minimum 4 feet deep, installed 5 feet from equipment). The landscape plan and electrical plan must be cross-referenced to assess this requirement.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: Dumpster or waste collection locations are not shown on the electrical plan (Sheet 21), and the site plan (Sheet 9) does not clearly indicate whether dumpsters are adjacent to any transformer pad location. Without explicit documentation of dumpster positions and clearance dimensions from transformer pads, this requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if dumpsters adjacent)

comment: Bicycle parking racks are shown on detail sheet 22 (Construction Details 1) with spacing requirements, but no cross-reference is made to transformer pad locations on the electrical plan. Without transformer pads identified on the construction details or with dimensions marked from bike racks to transformer pads, the 5-foot minimum clearance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if bike racks adjacent)

comment: Light poles are not shown on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) in relation to transformer pad locations. A photometric plan is referenced in the review guide but not provided in the plan set. Without documentation of light pole positions and dimensions from any transformer pad, the 5-foot minimum clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if light poles adjacent)

comment: The fire protection plan (Sheet 10) designates fire lanes on the site, and the electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations, but no cross-reference or dimensions show whether any pad is within 15 feet of a fire lane. Without marked clearance dimensions or explicit distance callouts, compliance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if fire lanes designated)

comment: The utility tap plan (Sheet 19) shows water line routing for the site, and the electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations, but no cross-reference or dimensions show the clearance between any transformer pad and the water line. Without marked clearance dimensions or documented analysis of separation distances, compliance with the 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: The utility tap plan (Sheet 19) shows wastewater line routing, and the electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations, but no cross-reference or dimensions show the clearance between any transformer pad and the wastewater line. Without marked clearance dimensions, compliance with the 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: The storm sewer plan (Sheet 12) shows storm drain line routing, and the electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations, but no cross-reference or dimensions show the clearance between any transformer pad and the storm drain line. Without marked clearance dimensions, compliance with the 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: The electrical plan shows transformer pad locations, and the utility tap plan shows various utility lines (water, wastewater, storm drain, and references to electric conduit), but no cross-sections or dimension callouts show the vertical and horizontal separations between transformer pads and other underground utilities. The minimum 12-inch clearance requirement (both horizontal and vertical, outside diameter to outside diameter) cannot be verified without marked dimensions or cross-sections.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: The electrical plan shows transformer pad locations, and the site plan shows building footprints, but no cross-sections or analysis documents whether transformer locations are positioned above, below, or near other utility lines, or whether any building foundations are constructed over Austin Energy underground facilities. Without cross-sections or documented utility coordination, this requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: No overhead distribution line routing is shown on the electrical plan or other plan sheets. The plan indicates 'Overhead Electric' as part of the site context but does not provide detailed overhead line routing, conductor locations, or heights. Without overhead line documentation, the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance requirement cannot be verified. A utility plan or overhead line detail sheet is needed.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if overhead distribution lines present)

comment: Overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors are not specifically mapped or detailed on the electrical plan. The plan references 'Overhead Electric' but does not show conductor routing, pole locations, conductor heights, or 15-foot radius clearance zones. Without detailed overhead line documentation, compliance with the 15-foot radial clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads and proposed facilities (if overhead distribution primary/neutral conductors present)

comment: The electrical plan does not indicate whether any transformer pad is located in a niche (accessible from outside but within building footprint), enclosed area, or notched-out building configuration. No cross-section drawings demonstrating vertical clearances within niche access paths are provided. Without this documentation, the applicability and compliance status of the 35-foot vertical clearance requirement cannot be determined.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if in niche configuration)

comment: The electrical plan does not identify any niche service installations. No architectural specifications showing 3-hour fire wall ratings are provided in the plan set. No electrical plan notes document consultation with Austin Energy Design business unit regarding niche configurations. Without documentation of niche service proposal and its associated requirements, this item cannot be evaluated.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if niche service proposed)

comment: The site plan shows no overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas directly above transformer pad locations. However, no cross-section sheets are provided in the plan set to demonstrate or verify vertical clearances in any access paths. If any pads are located under covered areas, overhangs, or have access paths through structures, cross-sections must be provided. The absence of cross-sections prevents verification of this requirement.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.10.3 (survey requirement as required by AE Design)
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas present above)

comment: The electrical plan does not identify whether transformer equipment is oil-filled or dry-type. The grading plan (Sheet 11) shows general site drainage contours but does not specifically address drainage direction around transformer pad locations or indicate whether pads have level pads or sloped bases. Without equipment type specification and without grading callouts at transformer locations, compliance with the requirement that liquid flow must be away from buildings cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if oil-filled equipment)

comment: Transformer pads are shown on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) but are NOT depicted on the plat (Sheet 2). Because transformer pad locations are not shown on the plat in relation to property lines, easements, or public right-of-way, it is impossible to verify that all five pads are 100% on private property and not in public right-of-way or straddling property lines. This is a critical documentation gap—transformer locations must be shown on the plat with confirmation of private property location.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: The plat (Sheet 2) identifies several easements including drainage, utility, and wastewater easements across the site. The electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations but does not indicate whether any pad is located within drainage easements, water easements, sewer easements, or electrical easements under overhead lines. Without explicit clearance of all pads from these prohibited easement areas, and without documented Austin Energy Design written approval for any pad within an easement, compliance cannot be verified.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 4 (property requirement); easement-specific regulations
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: The electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations but does not depict transformer easements around the pads. The plat (Sheet 2) does not show transformer easements. Without easement areas drawn on the plat identifying access rights for Austin Energy personnel and equipment, and without documented easement widths determined by Austin Energy Design, this requirement cannot be verified. Transformer easements must be explicitly shown and dimensioned.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.10.3 (additional clearance and access easements may be required)
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: The electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations and references underground electric lines but does not clearly depict the complete routing of conduits/cables from each transformer pad to associated meters or service disconnects. The plat does not show electrical routing or confirm that routing is 100% on private property. Without explicit documentation of electrical routing paths and their location on private property, this requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads and electrical routing

comment: The electrical plan identifies five transformer pads but does not reference Austin Energy Design-approved pad detail sheets. No pad dimensions (length × width) are shown on the plans, and no service type specification (single-phase vs. three-phase) is identified. Without explicit reference to AE Design-approved transformer pad details and without specification of service type, it is impossible to verify that pad dimensions match AE Design requirements for the applicable service configuration.
codeCitations: UCM § 1.18.0 (obtain transformer pad detail from AE Design)
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

comment: All five transformer pads are located immediately adjacent to (within 4 feet of) parking areas, drive aisles, or vehicle circulation routes. However, no bollards (4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts) are shown or specified anywhere on the electrical plan or detail sheets. No detail drawing reference is provided for bollard installation per AE Design equipment pad details. This represents a violation of UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4, which requires bollards when pads are within 4 feet of parking/vehicle areas.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pads (Pads 1-5 located within parking areas and drive aisles)

comment: Overhead distribution facilities are referenced on the electrical plan as 'Overhead Electric' but are not detailed showing conductor routing, pole locations, heights, or clearance envelopes. No documentation exists showing whether buildings, parking garages, light poles, signs, billboards, chimneys, antennas, or tanks are installed under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities. Without detailed overhead line routing and clearance documentation, this prohibition cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads and proposed site structures/equipment (if overhead distribution facilities present)
